There was no explanation because there was none needed.Tell me, during that game, when did you need to know what "Cover" did? 

 

From the very first moment we turned over the card on our very first turn.  

"Do we have to DO something to make the 'cover' aspect of the card work?"  

"Do we have to declare that we are taking cover behind it?"  

"Are objects considered a different type of card than creatures or people?"

"Does cover mean that any damage we do is first applied to the cover item and that it must be destroyed before damage passes through to the intended target?"  

 

"Dinosaur" or "drone" implies something attacking you or that you attack.  "Cover" implies something you can hide behind or that blocks you from attacking something else.  

 

It's one thing to set things up to avoid having to create and print a large rule book or constantly-expanding glossary.  I totally get that, lol.  Not an issue.  I also get that the designers of this game don't have time to maintain a list of the words that are associated with this game for people that might have a question about if they're understanding a card word correctly.   I'm just baffled that there's opposition to the existence of a list like this or that anyone could think that it's totally unnecessary.  Here's how simple a list it is:

Acrobat, Agent, Amazon, Ammo, Anomaly, Appendage, Bounty, Burst, Cavalier, Citizen, Clue, Cohort, Component, Cover, Crew, Cryptid, Cultist, Demon, Device, Dinosaur, Distortion, Diversion, Dreadnaught, Drone, Drug, Elemental, Flagship, Flying Ace, Forensic Scientist, Fowl, Gun, Gunman, Harmony, Inmate, Instrument, Jinx, The Law, Lord of the Underworld, Lucky, Mechanical Golem, Melody, Minion, Mode, Module, Mummy, Musketeer, Nest, Plating, Primeval Limb, Private Eye, Projection, Rat, Relic, Rhythm, Ronin, Spell, Style, Thorathian, Thug, Timeship, Time Portal, Tool, Train, Trap, Treasure, Trial, Underboss, Vat, Victim, Viking, Voodoo Pin and Zombie

 

I mean, that's it.  That's all that was needed.   And that's all that IS needed, lol.  Now when someone does a search for ANY of these keywords, THIS post will be one of the results.   No matter which keyword they may have been looking for (and not finding in the Glossary), this list and this discussion now exists to clarify that these keywords are all circumstantial and based on other cards that may come into play.  None of these keywords indicate any special sort of power or gameplay rule.  They merely indicate a specific target for some of the villain or environment cards that may come into play.  

 

Prior to this discussion there wasn't anything anywhere in the rules or online that clarified in one easy place this category of card words.

 

And thanks Spiff, I probably WILL update the wiki if someone hasn't already done it.   

 

 

(I put in extra words and extra explanation in this posting to further aid in someone doing a Google search)

If a player has a problem understanding something, then that's a problem. But you're the first person to raise this problem, which implies that it's really not very common.

A list of keywords in the rulebook is kind of useless, since the statement that keywords only have meaning circumstantially has exactly the same meaning as a list of keywords would. In fact, it could actually be harmful; whenever a new expansion comes out, the list becomes incomplete. Thus, the fix to your problem is to make the existing statement in the rulebook more prominent. And if, of the tiny minority of people who may suffer from this problem, one of them still misses this bit of text, and do a search for 'cover' or 'train' or what have you... well, a list exists now. That's a thing, it's here and it's on the wiki, and people who try to find it will be able to.
